;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Syrian opposition]] groups backed by [[Turkey]] recapture the strategic city of [[Saraqib]], lift the siege on four Turkish observation points and cut the [[Transport in Syria#Motorways|M5 highway]]. [http://www.syriahr.com/en/?p=155907 (SOHR)] [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-02/27/c_138824419.htm (Xinhua)] 
**A [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish]] [[sniper]] kills a [[Syrian Army|Syrian]] [[lieutenant colonel]] in Syria's [[Tell Abyad District|Tell Abyad countryside]]. [http://www.syriahr.com/?p=365438 (SOHR)]
**Three [[Turkish Army|Turkish soldier]]s are killed in Syrian Army attacks in [[Idlib]], bringing the number of Turkish soldiers killed in Syria to 21. [https://www.jpost.com/Breaking-News/Erdogan-says-three-more-Turkish-soldiers-killed-in-Syrias-Idlib-619073 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**36 Syrian Army troops and 25 Turkish-backed rebels are killed, bringing the total death toll in Idlib since December to 1,186 opposition fighters and 1,136 [[Government of Syria|Syrian government]] soldiers. [http://www.syriahr.com/en/?p=155946 (SOHR)]
**[[2020 Balyun airstrikes|Airstrikes]] kill at least 33 [[Turkish Land Forces|Turkish troops]] and injures 39 others in [[Jabal Zawiya]], [[Idlib Governorate]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/erdogan-convenes-emergency-meeting-over-idlib-tensions/news (''Daily Sabah'')] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-51667717 (BBC News)]
**Turkey says it has 'neutralized' 1,709 Syrian government elements in Idlib since 10 February 2020 and that it has destroyed 55 [[tank]]s, 3 [[Military helicopter|helicopters]], 18 [[Armored fighting vehicle|armored vehicles]], 29 [[howitzer]]s, 21 [[military vehicle]]s, 4 [[Anti-aircraft warfare|Docka anti-aircraft guns]], 6 [[Ammunition dump|ammunition depots]] and 7 [[Mortar (weapon)|mortars]] in the operations. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkey/turkey-neutralizes-1-709-regime-elements-in-idlib-syria/1747480 (Anadolu Agency)]
**Turkey opens its [[Syria–Turkey border|border with Syria]] and allows [[Refugees of the Syrian Civil War|Syrian refugees]] free passage to [[Europe]] effective immediately for the next 72 hours. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/turkey-syrian-refugees-free-passage-europe-soldiers-killed-Idlib (''Middle East Eye'')]
**Turkish Foreign Minister [[Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu]] and [[Secretary General of NATO|NATO Secretary General]] [[Jens Stoltenberg]] hold talks amid the escalation in Idlib with Syria and [[Russia]]. [https://apnews.com/9dd7b9b3674a5a635f789c0d9489cc66 (AP)]
**[[Twitter]], [[Facebook]] and [[Instagram]] are blocked in Turkey, while [[YouTube]] and [[WhatsApp]] are partially restricted. It is understood that the measures are intended to protect details surrounding troop and equipment deployments. [https://netblocks.org/reports/social-media-blocked-in-turkey-as-idlib-military-crisis-escalates-r8VWGXA5 (Netblocks)]
*A cyber attack in [[Australia]] forces the cancellation of wool sales across the country. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/rural/2020-02-27/ransomware-cyber-attack-cripples-australian-wool-sales/12007912 (ABC AU)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] enters [[Correction (stock market)|correction territory]] after plunging 700 points at opening. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2020/02/27/dow-markets-plunge-correction-coronavirus/4889977002/ (''USA Today'')]
**[[Stock market|Markets]] are on pace for their worst week since the [[Financial crisis of 2007–08|2008 financial crisis]]. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-dow-is-on-track-for-its-worst-weekly-slide-since-the-2008-financial-crisis-2020-02-27 (''Market Watch'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
***[[Vice Presidency for Women and Family Affairs|Vice President for Family Affairs]] [[Masoumeh Ebtekar]] is infected with the novel coronavirus. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/state-newspaper-says-masoumeh-ebtekar-iran-vice-president-and-spokeswoman-for-1979-hostage-takers-has-new-virus/2020/02/27/a1c88fde-5969-11ea-8efd-0f904bdd8057_story.html (''Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
***236 more coronavirus cases are confirmed in [[Italy]], bringing the number to 655. Five more virus-related deaths are confirmed, bringing the death toll in the country to seventeen. Forty-five people recovered from the disease. [https://www.repubblica.it/cronaca/2020/02/22/news/coronavirus_in_italia_aggiornamento_ora_per_ora-249241616/amp/ (''La Repubblica'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***A woman is diagnosed with the coronavirus after a possible person-to-person transmission. It would be the first case of transmission in the United States with no known contacts to overseas cases. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/coronavirus-cdc-didn-t-immediately-test-covid-19-case-n1143996 (NBC)]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] temporarily suspends entry to the kingdom for the [[Umrah]] Islamic pilgrimage and visits to al [[Al-Masjid an-Nabawi]] in [[Medina]] due to fears over the spread of the deadly novel coronavirus. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-saudi/saudi-arabia-suspends-entry-for-umrah-visits-to-al-masjid-al-nabawy-amid-coronavirus-idUSKCN20K3CQ (Reuters)]
**Saudi Arabia blocks all foreign pilgrims from entering the country. This block happens just before the [[Ramadan]] fasting. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-02-28/saudi-arabia-bans-foreign-pilgrims-amid-coronavirus/12008894 (ABC AU)]
**[[Prime Minister of Japan]] [[Shinzo Abe]] announces that all junior and high schools will be asked to close from March 2 until their upcoming spring break to help fight the coronavirus pandemic. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-japan/pm-abe-asks-all-japans-schools-to-close-over-coronavirus-idUSKCN20L0BI (Reuters)]
**[[Estonia]] confirms their first case. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/countries-confirmed-cases-coronavirus-200125070959786.html (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Greece]] confirms its second and third cases and cancels all [[Carnival#Greece|Carnival]]-related events. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-greece-idUSKCN20L1F3 (Reuters)]
**The first case in [[San Marino]] is confirmed. [https://www.altarimini.it/News132152-coronavirus-primo-caso-nella-repubblica-di-san-marino.php (''Alta Rimini'')] 
*The decision to build a [[third runway]] at [[Heathrow Airport]] is found to be unlawful by the [[Court of Appeal of England and Wales|Court of Appeal]] because the [[British government]] did not take into account its commitments under the [[Paris Agreement]] to [[Climate change mitigation|combat climate change]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-51658693 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**A senior Turkish official tells [[Reuters]] that Turkey "will no longer stop Syrian refugees from reaching Europe". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security/turkey-with-more-dead-troops-wont-stop-syrian-refugees-reaching-europe-official-idUSKCN20L0GQ (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*Astronomers discover the largest known explosion ever in the [[history of the Universe]], which occurred in the [[Ophiuchus]] galaxy cluster. It replaces [[MS 0735.6+7421]]. As space and ground telescopes that study radio emissions improve (which are better than X-ray observations for detecting these), more similar explosions, or "giant radio fossils", may be found. [https://phys.org/news/2020-02-astronomers-biggest-explosion-history-universe.html (Phys)] [https://www.cnn.com/2020/02/27/world/biggest-explosion-black-hole-universe-scn/index.html (CNN)] [https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.01291 (Astrophysics via arXiv at Cornell University)]
